note: Named executives are limited to individuals explicitly verifiable in sources.json/signals.json. Buying centers referenced without a named individual are listed under target_functions WITHOUT fabricated names. FACT / AI HYPOTHESIS / RECOMMENDATION are separated.

executives.name: Belen Garijo
executives.fact: Belen Garijo became Sanofi CEO effective April 29, 2026, succeeding ousted CEO Paul Hudson, after shares fell ~25% over the prior year amid underwhelming trial updates.
executives.ai_hypothesis: A new CEO installed after a stalled turnaround will likely reset strategic priorities, scrutinize vendor spend and re-evaluate commercial and R&D partnerships within her first two to three quarters.
executives.indegene_angle: Incumbent vendor relationships tied to the prior regime are exposed to review, but the new team opens a window to re-pitch DAAI, Omnichannel and MedComm value against Garijo's incoming agenda.
executives.why_it_matters: A new CEO reviewing vendor spend creates the rarest commercial window — re-pitch now or wait out her full first-year agenda.
executives.engagement_recommendation: Map current Company stakeholders against the new leadership structure and prepare a value-reaffirmation briefing timed to Garijo's first 100 days.

executives.name: Olivier Charmeil
executives.fact: Olivier Charmeil served as interim CEO between Paul Hudson's departure (last day Feb 17, 2026) and Belen Garijo's start (April 29, 2026).
executives.ai_hypothesis: As a bridge leader, Charmeil is unlikely to authorize major new vendor commitments; strategic decisions defer to the incoming CEO.
executives.indegene_angle: Maintain relationship continuity during the interim period without expecting large new mandates until Garijo sets direction.
executives.why_it_matters: Interim leaders do not authorise mandates — staying warm now positions Company the moment Garijo sets direction.
executives.engagement_recommendation: Keep engagement warm and informational through the interim; time substantive proposals to post-Garijo transition.

executives.name: Paul Hudson
executives.fact: Paul Hudson was ousted after seven years as CEO, his last day February 17, 2026, following underwhelming trial updates and a ~25% share decline.
executives.ai_hypothesis: Relationships anchored to Hudson's tenure carry elevated churn risk as the new regime reassesses commitments.
executives.indegene_angle: Do not anchor future outreach to Hudson-era relationships; reframe value for the incoming leadership.
executives.why_it_matters: Hudson-era relationships carry elevated churn risk as the new regime reassesses commitments — flag them before they become surprises.
executives.engagement_recommendation: No engagement. Audit any Hudson-era stakeholder dependencies for continuity risk.

executives.name: Frederic Oudea
executives.fact: Frederic Oudea is Chairman, overseeing the CEO transition from Hudson to Garijo.
executives.ai_hypothesis: As Chairman through a contentious CEO change, Oudea's board is signaling a demand for improved execution and disciplined capital allocation.
executives.indegene_angle: Board-level focus on execution and cost discipline supports Company's efficiency and launch-velocity value narrative.
executives.why_it_matters: The board drove a CEO change over execution concerns — every proposal must now prove measurable execution and cost outcomes.
executives.engagement_recommendation: Frame proposals around measurable execution improvement and cost efficiency consistent with board priorities.

target_functions.basis_fact: Dupixent is ~45% of quarterly revenue (€5.2bn Q2 2026) with a rapid indication cadence (bullous pemphigoid, CSU adult and pediatric).
target_functions.indegene_angle: A repeatable Omnichannel/MedComm/MLR engine across successive indications plus competitive defense against emerging AD entrants (Amgen rocatinlimab).
target_functions.why_it_matters: Dupixent is ~45% of quarterly revenue with a rapid indication cadence — each approval compounds launch workload, and Amgen's entrant makes speed a defense.
target_functions.engagement_recommendation: Propose a standing indication-launch playbook Company executes on each new Dupixent approval, plus a competitive-defense analytics program.

target_functions.function: Rare Disease / new-brand launch leadership (Wayrilz, Qfitlia, Cablivi)
target_functions.basis_fact: Multiple first-in-class rare-disease approvals across US, EU and China (first BTK inhibitor for ITP; first US therapy for hemophilia A/B).
target_functions.indegene_angle: Greenfield multi-region launches across Omnichannel, MedComm, MLR and Regulatory ops.
target_functions.why_it_matters: First-in-class approvals across US, EU and China mean simultaneous multi-region launch waves — greenfield capacity is needed now, not after launch.
target_functions.engagement_recommendation: Target the Wayrilz and Qfitlia launches with a global launch-excellence proposal spanning US, EU and China.

target_functions.basis_fact: Sanofi is building a proprietary AI ecosystem (Snowflake/ElementumAI data partnerships; earlier Formation Bio and OpenAI) toward becoming the first biopharma powered by AI at scale.
target_functions.indegene_angle: DAAI/Tech Solutions inflection point — position as a life-sciences-specialized AI partner for commercialization-specific use cases rather than risk disintermediation.
target_functions.why_it_matters: Sanofi is building its own AI ecosystem at scale — Company either anchors commercialization-specific AI use cases now or gets disintermediated.
target_functions.engagement_recommendation: Develop a POV on complementing Sanofi's proprietary AI with commercialization-specific AI use cases.
